channel.description: Latest articles from The Garden Island (thegardenisland.com)

item.title: 25 acres of Poipu on the auction block
item.description: LIHUE — Bids are currently being accepted for a 25-acre site on Kauai’s South Shore.

item.title: EDITORIAL: State must counter EPA rule rollback
item.description: Americans who prefer clean air to air laden with greenhouse gases (atmosphere-warming pollutants) and other toxins have been sold out by President Donald Trump’s decision to revoke the Environmental Protection Agency’s 2009 “endangerment finding.”

item.title: ISLAND HISTORY: Valdemar L’Orange Knudsen and a peek at old Poipu
item.description: Born at Waiawa, Kauai, Valdemar L’Orange Knudsen (1910-1990) was the son of Cecilia L’Orange Knudsen and rancher and legislator Eric Knudsen, who gained fame as the “Teller of Hawaiian Tales” on the KTOH Lihue radio program he hosted during World War II.

item.title: Illegal rentals hurt Hawaii’s hotel sector, industry leaders says
item.description: Honolulu’s hotel sector pumps more than $12 billion a year into the local economy and supports nearly 64,000 jobs, a new study says, but industry leaders warn those gains are increasingly at risk as illegal vacation rentals drain housing from residents and erode public support for tourism.

item.title: Happy Camper for Saturday, February 21, 2026
item.description: Lowell High School, located in San Francisco, Calif., is the “oldest public high school west of the Mississippi” after being founded in 1856. Lowell High School baseball team is one of the participants in the Kauai High School preseason baseball tournament that opened play on Thursday when Lowell beat the host Red Raiders following a Kauai pitching change (everybody gets a chance during preseason).

item.title: Lei legislation aims to bolster Hawaii flower farm industry
item.description: Buying lei made only with natural materials from Hawaii nei could be a new requirement for state agencies under an effort at the Legislature aimed at helping the local floriculture industry.

item.title: Las Vegas sees sharp visitor drop as leisure spending wanes
item.description: LAS VEGAS — On Fridays, it still feels like peak Vegas — rolling suitcases, packed rideshare queues and the familiar churn at Harry Reid International. By Monday, the airport has quieted considerably.

item.title: Free tax services come to Kukui Grove
item.description: LIHUE — The service is free, and available today at the Kukui Grove Center.

item.title: Kauai secures $7.5 million in federal funding
item.description: LIHUE — Hawaii’s federal delegation secured $7.5 million in federal funding for housing and transportation projects on Kauai through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process, the County of Kauai announced Friday.
